'''Fukagawa Shrine''' (ふかがわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Fukagawa-chō|Q99541288|qid=Q99541288|lt=Fukagawa-chō}}, {{ill|Seto, Aichi|Q499493|qid=Q499493}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} identified with "Fukagawa Shrine" in Yamada District, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'.

=== History ===
Until the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, it was called '''Hachiōji''' and served as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of {{ill|Seto|Q119658043|qid=Q119658043|lt=Seto Village}}. Shrine tradition says it was founded in {{ill|771|Q29950|qid=Q29950}} by inviting {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsukami}} deities. There is a horizontal-chamber {{ill|Round Kofun|Q11394747|qid=Q11394747}} in the precincts. {{ill|Amano Sadakage|Q6535030|qid=Q6535030}} identified it as the Yamada District "Fukagawa Shrine" of the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}},' and this became the accepted view. According to '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Owari Junkōki}},' there was a stream called Irikawa east of the shrine, formerly called "Fukagawa." There are almost no alternate views against identifying this shrine as Fukagawa Shrine, and scholars such as {{ill|Tsuda Masanari|Q22123474|qid=Q22123474}} also support this. On divine rank, the '{{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|Q11041830|qid=Q11041830}}' has "Junior Third Upper Fukagawa Tenjin" in the Jōji manuscript and "Junior Third Fukagawa Tenjin" in the Genki manuscript.

On a temple bell once at this shrine's {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} with the inscription {{ill|Eikyō|Q1193059|qid=Q1193059}} 10 ({{ill|1438|Q6377|qid=Q6377}}), appears: "Seto Village in Yamada District, Owari; Ise Amaterasu Daijingū, Hakusan Myōri Kangen, this is the Hachiōji bell ... great donor Zuiryū Shūhaku," suggesting it was already called "Hachiōji" in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Muromachi period}}. It is said that when {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}} visited during falconry, he was nearly attacked by an assassin of {{ill|Saitō Tatsuoki|Q2880879|qid=Q2880879}} of Mino, but escaped thanks to the chief priest's quick action, and in thanks received 75 koku of offering rice. The oldest surviving {{ill|Munafuda|Q8008834|qid=Q8008834}} is from {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 1 ({{ill|1596|Q6785|qid=Q6785}}), said to date from rebuilding at the current site after a fire. Several other 17th-century munafuda also survive. In the early-Edo '{{ill|Kanbunmuramuraoboegaki|Q137766629|qid=Q137766629}},' it reads "Seto Village ... Hachiōji ... formerly tax-exempt." The Ninomiya family served as {{ill|Shinkan (official)|Q11589454|qid=Q11589454}} from old times, and '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Owari Junkōki}}' records "priest Ninomiya Jibū-dayū."

There are three {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}}: first torii (approach entrance), second torii (precinct entrance), and third torii (in front of haiden)<ref name="chunichi.co.jp20131208"/>. The first torii was built in {{ill|1915|Q2084|qid=Q2084}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 4), removed in {{ill|2000|Q1985|qid=Q1985}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 12) due to collapse risk, and rebuilt in {{ill|2014|Q1999|qid=Q1999}} (Heisei 26)<ref name="chunichi.co.jp20131208"/>.

The precincts were sometimes used as an entertainment venue. On {{ill|February 28|Q2362|qid=Q2362}}, {{ill|1943|Q18623|qid=Q18623}} (Shōwa 18), a fire broke out at Ishibashi acrobat troupe grounds there, killing five spectators and injuring 29<ref>{{Cite book |和書 |editor=Nichigai Associates editorial dept. |title=Japan Disaster History Encyclopedia 1868-2009 |publisher=Nichigai Associates |year=2010-09-27 |page=61 |isbn=9784816922749}}</ref>.

=== Cultural properties ===
; {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}
* Ceramic {{ill|Komainu|Q20155846|qid=Q20155846}}<ref>{{Cite web|和書|date= |url=http://www.pref.aichi.jp/kyoiku/bunka/bunkazainavi/yukei/kougei/kunisitei/0428.html |title=Ceramic Komainu, Honden |publisher=Aichi Prefecture |accessdate=2013-05-27}}</ref> - A {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}} work. Shrine tradition says this is Japan's oldest ceramic komainu, made by Seto pottery ancestor {{ill|Kagemasa Kato|Q11399278|qid=Q11399278}} (Shirōzaemon, Tōshirō).

; Seto City tangible cultural properties
* Honden<ref>{{Cite web|和書|date=2011-03-28 |url=http://www.city.seto.aichi.jp/docs/2011012500028/ |title=Fukagawa Shrine Honden |publisher=Seto City |accessdate=2013-05-27}}</ref> - built in the {{ill|Bunka|Q1373146|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka period}} of the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, by {{ill|Tatekawa Washirō|Q65277448|qid=Q65277448}} of {{ill|Suwa Region|Q11631849|qid=Q11631849|lt=Suwa}}.
* Tōhiko Shrine (honden, heiden, haiden, tsuiji wall)
* {{ill|Bonshō|Q8192099|qid=Q8192099}}<ref>{{Cite web|和書|date=2011-03-28 |url=http://www.city.seto.aichi.jp/docs/2011012500011/ |title=Bonshō with Eikyō inscription |publisher=Seto City |accessdate=2013-05-27}}</ref> - made in the {{ill|Eikyō|Q1193059|qid=Q1193059}} era of the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, evidence of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}.
* Oribe lantern<ref>{{Cite web|和書|date=2011-03-28 |url=http://www.city.seto.aichi.jp/docs/2011012400090/ |title=Oribe lantern |publisher=Seto City |accessdate=2013-05-27}}</ref>

=== Annual rites ===
* Jan 1 - New Year's Day festival
* Jan 5 - First Ebisu festival
* Feb 3 - Setsubun festival
* Feb 17 - Kinen festival
* 3rd Sunday of April - Tōso festival
* Jun 30 - Nagoshi great purification
* Oct 15 - Annual festival
* Nov 23 - Niiname festival
* Dec 31 - Great purification
